Our Buildings team delivers projects across a broad range of sectors including health, education, defence, multi-residential, retail and commercial developments. Working alongside experienced engineers, designers and technical specialists, you'll play an important role in developing coordinated, practical and buildable civil design solutions.
Our culture has a strong focus on learning, personal development and collaboration. You'll be supported by experienced professionals who are passionate about mentoring and helping individuals grow their technical and professional capabilities.
Day to day tasks would involve:
- Prepare civil engineering documentation for building and site development projects using established drafting standards and procedures.

- Ensure drawings comply with applicable standards, project requirements and quality procedures.
- Assist with managing drawing registers and project deliverables.
- Identify and resolve drafting and coordination issues to support efficient project delivery.
- Deliver project outcomes within client specifications and expectations
To be successful for this role you'll need:
- Tertiary qualification in Computer Aided Design or relevant experience
- Minimum of 2 years of drafting experience in an engineering consultancy as a civil drafter
- Familiarity with local authority and state government approval and regulatory requirement
- Experience in the operation of software design tools such as AutoCAD packages
- Experience producing civil drafting documentation for buildings, site development or infrastructure projects.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with an eye for detail and a strong focus on the production of quality outputs
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Ongoing commitment to professional development through self-study, training and seminars, and maintaining your Continual Professional Development (CPD)

- Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

The Stantec community unites approximately 34,000 employees working in over 450+ locations across six continents. So, when we take on a project, we see the opportunity to make a lasting connection with the people and places where we live and work.

About the Role
PCP Solutions is seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Graduate Civil Engineer to join our growing team.

Working alongside experienced Project Managers, Site Engineers and Supervisors, you will assist with the planning, coordination, quality assurance and delivery of civil construction works from commencement through to completion.
The successful applicant will be provided with ongoing guidance and support while developing their technical knowledge, project management skills and practical understanding of civil construction operations.
The Company
PCP Solutions is a leading civil earthworks and commercial plumbing business based in Toowoomba, delivering projects across South East Queensland.
With over 70 staff, PCP Solutions specialises in large-scale infrastructure works for Tier 1 contractors whilst maintaining a supportive, family-focused culture.
We pride ourselves on delivering quality projects, building strong working relationships and providing opportunities for our employees to grow and develop within the business.
Key Responsibilities
Working under the guidance of senior project personnel, your responsibilities will include:
- Assist with daily site inspections and monitoring construction activities.
- Prepare, maintain and complete Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs) and associated quality assurance documentation.
- Assist with the preparation and submission of project reports and documentation to Principal Contractors.
- Support daily work front reporting, progress tracking and construction records.
- Assist with project programming, scheduling and monitoring critical deadlines.
- Provide project administration and engineering support to Project Managers, Site Engineers, Supervisors and Quality and Safety personnel.
- Assist with reviewing construction drawings, specifications and technical documentation.
- Monitor supplier material conformance and ensure materials meet project specifications.
- Assist with quantity calculations, material take-offs and procurement requirements.
- Support the implementation and maintenance of project quality, workplace health and safety and environmental controls.
- Assist with identifying and reporting potential project risks, delays and construction issues.
- Maintain accurate project records, filing systems and document control processes.
- Provide regular project progress updates to the Project Manager and wider project team.
- Ensure compliance with the company's Integrated Management System (IMS), policies and procedures.
Skills and Qualifications
We are looking for someone who is eager to learn, takes initiative and is passionate about developing a career in civil construction.
The successful applicant will ideally possess:
- A completed Bachelor's Degree in Civil Engineering or a related engineering discipline.
- Recent graduates and applicants with up to 2 years of industry experience are encouraged to apply.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work professionally with clients, suppliers, subcontractors and site personnel.
- Excellent organisational and time management skills.
- Strong attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate documentation.
- A willingness to learn and develop practical construction and project management skills.
- Basic understanding of civil construction methods, engineering drawings and specifications.
- Sound computer skills, including Microsoft Office applications.
- Ability to work independently when required and contribute positively to a team environment.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and a strong commitment to workplace safety.
- A current driver's licence and Construction White Card, or willingness to obtain a White Card prior to commencing.
- Willingness to travel to regional project locations as required.
Previous experience in civil construction, earthworks, water infrastructure or quality assurance will be highly regarded but is not essential.
What We Offer
- Opportunity to gain hands-on experience on major civil infrastructure projects.
- Mentoring and ongoing support from experienced engineering and construction professionals.
- Exposure to Tier 1 construction projects and industry-leading systems.
- Career development and progression opportunities within a growing company.
- A supportive, family-focused team environment.
- Competitive remuneration based on qualifications and experience.
- A diverse role offering both site-based and project administration experience.
How to Apply
If you are a motivated Graduate Civil Engineer looking to kick-start your career and gain practical experience in the civil construction industry, we would love to hear from you.
Apply via SEEK or email your resume and cover letter to admin@pcpsolutions.com.au

About Spiire

We bring together civil and water engineers, landscape architects, construction consultants, surveyors, town planners and urban designers to support the property and infrastructure sectors.
With over 430 employees, we’re one of Australia’s largest employee-owned property and infrastructure consultancies, bringing over 40 years of experience and local expertise to projects across Melbourne, Bendigo, Brisbane, Adelaide, Canberra, Geelong, Ballarat, Shepparton, Gippsland, Albury and Wodonga, and Townsville.

You’ll bring experience in urban development civil engineering design, with an interest in working across the different elements of land development. From roads and drainage to earthworks and servicing, you’ll help develop practical, coordinated designs that support projects from concept through to detailed documentation and delivery.
Working closely with our local team and supported by Spiire’s broader network, you’ll take responsibility for work that reflects your experience and strengths. We’re open to Civil Designers with an established foundation in design through to experienced practitioners looking for variety and the opportunity to contribute to a growing team.
This role will see you:
 - Prepare civil engineering designs, drawings and documentation for urban development projects.
 - Contribute to road, drainage, earthworks and servicing design, considering authority requirements and practical construction outcomes.
 - Coordinate inputs from engineers, designers and other project disciplines.
 - Liaise with clients, consultants and authorities to progress designs and address technical requirements.
 - Help resolve design queries and provide engineering input as projects move into construction.
 - Manage agreed tasks, project priorities and timeframes, seeking technical advice when needed.
 - Build strong working relationships and contribute to Spiire’s growing presence in Townsville.
About you
You’re an established Civil Designer with relevant experience in civil infrastructure design, ideally within urban development consulting.
You’ll bring a practical understanding of how the different elements of a development fit together, along with the ability to prepare clear, accurate designs and work collaboratively to resolve project challenges.
You’ll bring:
 - Associates Degree in Civil Engineering is preferred however not mandatory
 - Experience designing civil infrastructure for urban development or land development projects.
 - AutoCAD skills, with experience using 12d highly regarded.
 - An understanding of relevant engineering standards, council requirements and authority approval processes.
 - The ability to prepare and interpret engineering drawings, calculations and technical documentation.
 - Clear communication skills and the ability to build positive relationships with colleagues, clients and project stakeholders.
 - A practical approach to problem-solving and the judgement to recognise when specialist input is needed.
 - The ability to organise your work, follow through on commitments and work with a degree of independence appropriate to your experience.
Experience across multiple aspects of civil design would be valued, as would exposure to construction delivery.
Make a local impact, backed by a broader team
This is an opportunity to contribute to Spiire’s growing Townsville team and see the impact of your work in the local community.
You’ll work closely with experienced local colleagues while drawing on the technical expertise and support of our broader network. As the team grows, you’ll have opportunities to broaden your project experience, take on responsibility and develop your career in a direction that suits your strengths.
Whether you’re already based in Townsville or looking to make the region your home, we’d love to hear from you.

You will contribute to transport planning, project development, design, delivery, maintenance and asset management activities, while building your capability under the guidance of senior engineering staff.

candidates.content_text:
ABOUT THE ROLE
Please read all information carefully before applying.
Under general direction, this position undertakes programmed and responsive inspections of Council’s road and associated infrastructure assets to identify defects, assess condition and collect accurate asset information.
The position supports the development and prioritisation of maintenance, renewal and construction programs by providing reliable inspection data, technical observations and recommendations to the Senior Technical Officer and relevant Infrastructure Services teams. The role is required to develop and maintain a sound working knowledge of Council’s infrastructure inspection programs, asset management systems, relevant standards, policies and procedures. The level of responsibility, independence and technical judgement exercised will reflect the classification level at which the incumbent is appointed.
Employment Status: Full Time, Permanent
Hours of Work: 72.50 hours per fortnight, nine (9) day fortnight
Award: Level 3 to 4 of the Queensland Local Government Industry (Stream A) Award – State 2017 / Charters Towers Regional Council Certified Agreement
Salary Range: $88,366 to $99,719 gross per annum, plus applicable allowances
Directorate: Infrastructure Services
Department: Operations
ABOUT YOU
The successful candidate will have:
| Essential Knowledge, skills and abilities |
Level 2 Essential:
- Demonstrated knowledge and capability in civil infrastructure, road construction, road maintenance, asset inspection or a closely related field, gained through relevant tertiary study and/or practical experience.
- Knowledge of infrastructure inspection and condition assessment principles, including identification and documentation of defects and development of appropriate recommendations within the scope of the position.
- Ability to inspect civil infrastructure, identify defects and deterioration, assess asset condition and accurately document findings.
- Ability to collect, interpret, analyse and accurately record technical and asset condition data and identify relevant trends, defects and emerging issues.
- Ability to undertake technical investigations using established methodologies and apply sound judgement appropriate to the classification level and the incumbent’s competency.
- Ability to use, or quickly develop proficiency in, electronic recordkeeping, asset management, GIS, inspection and similar technical information systems.
- Well-developed organisational skills with the ability to manage field inspection activities, competing priorities, deadlines and associated administrative requirements.
- Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear technical records and reports and communicate appropriately with internal and external stakeholders.
- Demonstrated commitment to professional and responsive customer service when dealing with infrastructure and community-related matters.
- Understanding of safe work practices associated with road environments, construction activities and field-based infrastructure inspections.
| Essential Education/Qualifications |
Level 3 Essential:
- Certificate III in Civil Construction or a similar field, or an equivalent combination of demonstrated relevant experience.
- Bridge Inspection Level 1.
- Bridge Inspection Level 2, or ability to obtain the required bridge inspection competency within six (6) months of appointment.
Level 4 Essential: (In addition to Level 3)
- Tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering, Asset Management, or a related discipline.
- Certificate IV in Civil Construction or a similar field, and/or an equivalent combination of demonstrated relevant experience.
- Bridge Inspection Level 2.
| Essential Licences |
Level 3 & 4 Essential:
- Possession and maintenance of a Queensland ‘C’ Class Driver Licence.
- General Construction Industry Certificate - White Card.
Progression: Progression from Level 3 to Level 4 is not automatic. It will be assessed by the Programming Assets Coordinator and People and Culture, based on evidence that the Level 4 criteria have been met as set out in this position description and that the incumbent is performing the full range of key responsibilities to a satisfactory standard.
BENEFITS
We have a range of benefits that include:
- Fortnightly RDO
- 5 weeks annual leave + 17.5% leave loading
- 3 weeks Personal/Carers Leave
- Domestic and Family Violence Leave
- Uniforms and PPE provided (if applicable to your role)
- Flexible Work Arrangements
- Annual wage progression
- 12% Superannuation
- Salary Sacrifice opportunities such as Remote Area Benefit
- Access to a range of learning and development opportunities, including on-the-job learning and formal training programs
- Employee Assistance Program
- Class 5 Vehicle rights while on call 
INHERENT REQUIREMENTS AND WORKING ENVIRONMENT
Inherent Requirements
The following are essential to performing this role safely. Council will consider reasonable adjustments to help a person meet these requirements.
- Work is split between the office and the field. Field work is outdoors across Council’s road network, including on and beside live roads and in remote parts of the region, with exposure to heat, sun, dust, noise, wildlife and wet weather. Officer duties involve using a computer, tablet and telephone, in the office and in the field, for extended periods to record inspections, update asset systems and prepare reports.
- Field work may involve working alone or in isolated locations, in line with Council’s safe work procedures for remote and isolated work.
- Be required to participate in an on-call roster, work outside ordinary hours, reasonable overtime and respond to emergencies and operational incidents including weekends, and emergency or disaster response, as reasonably directed to meet operational needs.
- Wear required personal protective equipment (PPE) for extended periods, including high-visibility clothing, safety boots and sun protection, and a hard hat and hearing and eye protection where required.
- Walk and stand for extended periods along road corridors, road shoulders, footpaths and drainage lines, including over uneven, loose, sloping or wet ground, to carry out inspections.
- Bend, kneel, squat, crouch and twist to inspect pavements, bridges, culverts and drainage structures, take measurements, and install or retrieve equipment at ground level.
- Climb embankments and creek banks and move through low-clearance areas such as beneath bridges and at culvert inlets and outlets, to inspect structures.
- Lift and carry light to moderate loads, such as traffic counters and road tubes, measuring equipment and signs, up to the maximum weight permitted under Council’s WHS manual handling requirements.
- Work safely on and beside live roads, including when installing or retrieving traffic-counting equipment, staying aware of passing traffic and operating plant and responding to warnings, signals and alarms.
- Have sufficient vision to identify and assess surface defects, cracking, deformation and other changes in asset condition, including during drive-by inspections.
- Drive a Council vehicle for extended periods, often over long distances and on unsealed roads, and get in and out of the vehicle frequently during inspections, to reach sites across the region.
Pre-Employment Checks, Health Monitoring and Immunisation
This position is required to complete a pre-employment medical assessment, including a drug and alcohol screen based on the inherent requirements above.
Council takes all reasonably practicable steps to provide a safe and healthy workplace and to prevent occupational disease. Under Council’s P0199 Vaccinations and Health Monitoring Procedure, this position is listed on Council’s health monitoring register as requiring Tetanus as a vaccination requirement for this position. 
MORE INFORMATION & QUESTIONS
Council is committed to building an inclusive culture that respects and promotes human rights and diversity and acknowledges that we respectfully journey together to aspire to be an inclusive and capable organisation. We are an equal employment opportunity employer and place value on our diverse workforce. We encourage applicants representing all genders, ethnicities, ages, languages, sexual orientations, people with a disability, and those with family responsibilities to apply.
As part of the selection process applicants may be required to undertake some or all of the following pre-employment assessments/check:
- Pre-employment medical including a drug & alcohol test
- National Police/Criminal History Check
- Right to Work in Australia Check
- Qualification/Licence Verification
Applications must be submitted online using the Apply Now link on this page and should include a cover letter and your current resume.
For further information, please view the Position Description.
For enquiries in relation to this vacancy, please contact Milad Alia – Manager Operations 07 4761 5300 or email. 
CLOSING DATE
11:59pm Sunday, 29 November 2026. 
Late applications will only be accepted at the discretion of the Chief Executive Officer.

About Flow
Flow Infrastructure is a specialist design and construct firm delivering water and wastewater treatment infrastructure, including water and sewage treatment plants, pump stations, recycled water schemes and industrial wastewater systems. Our sister company, Flow Utilities, operates and maintains the assets we deliver. Our clients include developers, councils, government and industry across South Australia and interstate.
Flow was established in 2026 by a team that has worked together for more than 20 years. Collectively we bring more than 80 years of experience and, in previous roles, our team delivered 37 sewage treatment plants, with project experience across Australia and New Zealand. Flow is certified to ISO 9001 and ISO 45001 and holds a building work contractors licence specific to sewer and water infrastructure installation.
Current projects include industrial and winery wastewater treatment, private water and sewerage schemes for greenfield communities, and municipal treatment plant upgrades, delivered for developers, industry, councils and government.
The role
You will prepare design and construction documentation across our water and wastewater projects, working jointly with our Design Lead on mechanical, piping and plant layout drafting and with our Electrical and Automation Lead on electrical and control documentation.
You will be involved from tender through detailed design, construction and as constructed records, working closely with our process and design engineers so that every drawing set is accurate, coordinated and buildable. You will:
- Prepare 2D drawings and 3D models for sewage and water treatment plants, pump stations, recycled water schemes and industrial wastewater systems.
- Produce general arrangements, plant layouts, piping arrangements and isometrics using AutoCAD and Plant 3D.
- Prepare tank, skid and fabrication drawings, along with valve, pump and instrument schedules.
- Prepare site layouts, pipeline and rising main alignments, long sections and services coordination drawings using Civil 3D.
- Draft P&IDs and process flow diagrams with our process engineers.
- Prepare electrical and control documentation, including single line diagrams, schematics, switchboard layouts and cable routes, under the direction of the Electrical and Automation Lead.
- Coordinate drawing inputs from suppliers, subcontractors and our civil and structural design partner.
- Prepare drawing sets for tenders, regulatory submissions, construction and as constructed records.
- Manage drawing registers and revision control, and help develop the CAD templates, blocks and standards for the business.
- Attend site during construction and commissioning as required, including measurement and as constructed checks.
About you
- Proven experience as a mechanical or process plant drafter. A Diploma or Advanced Diploma of Engineering (Drafting) is valued, but your portfolio matters more than your qualifications.
- At least 5 years of drafting experience in the water sector or comparable process plant work, ideally on water and wastewater treatment plants, pump stations or pipeline infrastructure. Applicants whose background is in residential, commercial building or architectural drafting are not suited to this position and will not be considered.
- Proficiency in AutoCAD, Civil 3D and Plant 3D is essential. Experience in Inventor or SolidWorks is an advantage.
- Construction experience is beneficial but not essential. It helps to understand how drawings turn into steel, pipe and concrete.
- Experience preparing P&IDs, piping arrangements and plant layouts, with a working knowledge of valves, pumps, pipework, instruments, tanks and dosing systems. Electrical and control drafting experience is highly regarded.
- Careful and organised, with good drawing control habits and a sound understanding of drafting standards.
- The ability to manage several projects at once.
- Clear communication skills, with the confidence to work with engineers, suppliers and site teams.
- Willing to undertake site visits within South Australia and occasional interstate travel as required.
What we offer
- A salary of $100k to $125k plus super, depending on experience.
- An equal share of company profits alongside every other permanent employee.
- Broad exposure across municipal and industrial water and wastewater projects, from design through construction and operation, with process, mechanical, electrical and automation design all delivered in house.
- Varied, hands on project work, and the opportunity to shape the drafting standards and templates of a growing business.
- A collaborative, experienced team where you work closely with the business owners and have a direct say in decisions.
- A modern office on Grote Street in the Adelaide CBD.
How to apply
Please include your CV, a cover letter and a selection of sample drawings or models with your application, with any confidential client information removed. Make sure your application accurately reflects your own experience and qualifications. Shortlisted candidates will be asked to talk through their work at interview and may be asked to complete a short practical drafting exercise. Applications that are clearly AI generated or overstate experience will not be progressed.
You must have current Australian working rights.

candidates.content_text:
Ready to take your land development experience to the next level?
Stantec Community Development team is looking for a Construction Engineer to join our Melbourne team, working across a diverse portfolio of land development and subdivision projects .
This is a hands-on role for an engineer who enjoys being close to construction, solving problems on site, working with contractors and clients, and helping projects move successfully from design through to delivery.
What you'll be doing
Working across residential and land development projects, you'll be responsible for:
- Providing contract administration throughout the construction phase
- Preparing, reviewing and managing tender documentation and submissions
- Assessing and managing variations, RFIs and contractor queries
- Undertaking site inspections and construction audits
- Auditing and signing off on water and sewer works and other civil infrastructure
- Identifying and resolving complex engineering and construction issues on site
- Preparing clear, professional engineering and construction reports
- Working closely with developers, contractors, consultants, authorities and other key stakeholders
- Helping ensure works are delivered in accordance with relevant designs, specifications and approval requirements
About you
We're looking for someone with:
- A degree in Civil Engineering or a related discipline
- Construction Engineering experience working on land development and subdivision projects
- Strong construction-phase and contract administration experience ideally using AS4000 or AS2124 Australian standard
- Practical knowledge of civil construction, particularly water, sewer and subdivision infrastructure
- Sewer and/or Water audit accreditation like SA1, WA1 and more
- Experience managing RFIs, variations, inspections and contractor interfaces
- Strong problem-solving skills and the confidence to resolve technical issues on site
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills
- The ability to balance technical quality, commercial considerations and project delivery
What we offer
We offer many benefits to ensure your professional development & wellbeing is ongoing.
- Genuine Flexible Working Arrangements - Including work from home opportunities, provision for school term contracts, job sharing and part time employment.
- Option to purchase up to 4 weeks additional leave.
- Learning and Talent Development Programs - Including Global programmes, online learning and on-the-job learning
- Professional Memberships, Salary Continuance Insurance (SCI), Service Recognition Awards
- Mental Health, Employee Assistance Program and Wellbeing Programs
About Stantec
The Stantec community unites approximately 34,000 employees working in over 450 locations across six continents. We collaborate across disciplines and industries to bring buildings, energy, resources, water, environmental, transport and infrastructure projects to life. Our work from initial project concept and planning through design, construction, and commissioning begins at the intersection of community, creativity, and client relationships.
Culture
Stantec is serious about healthy work-life balance, diversity, inclusion & equity, indigenous relations, innovation, community engagement, corporate sustainability, and social wellbeing. We have employee groups for women, LGBTQI , neurodiversity, and more! Our employees play sport, fundraise, volunteer, learn, and have fun together.
We are committed to reconciliation and to building respectful relationships with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. We’re better together when different perspectives are welcomed and valued, and we’re committed to a workplace where everyone can belong and thrive. candidates.title: Laboratory Technician (Casual)
candidates.abstract: Help deliver quality water to our community. Bring your problem-solving skills to a casual Laboratory Technician role and Rewrite the Future.
bullets: Ensure compliance with Drinking Water Guidelines & EPA licence conditions
Maintain laboratory standards, equipment, and operational integrity
Casual position working up to 35 hours per week
candidates.content_text:
The Laboratory Technician will play a crucial role in conducting analyses on water and wastewater. This position is vital for monitoring and protecting the Central Coast community and the environment. You will ensure compliance with Australian Drinking Water Guidelines, EPA Licence conditions, and ANZECC and other regulatory guidelines.
In addition to performing analyses, the Technician will maintain laboratory operations, assist in training staff, and contribute to quality assurance processes. Your analytical skills and attention to detail will create value for the community.
This position is required to provide quality customer service and create value for the community.
 Applicant Profile 
To be successful in this role, you will have:
- a degree qualification in Environmental, Chemistry or Natural Science or related field OR extensive contemporary experience in conducting analysis on water and wastewater, combined with ongoing professional development
- a current Class C Drivers Licence
- a valid Construction General Induction card - NSW SafeWork or equivalent
- a current Work Safely at Heights certification
- demonstrated experience in the collection, storage, preservation and routine analysis on samples of water and wastewater in accordance with accepted industry standards
- demonstrated experience in laboratory testing environment including methods for ensuring consistency and adherence to industry standard
- experience in communicating results of test analyses to appropriate staff and assist in the interpretation of results where appropriate and as required
- solid administrative skills which enable the incumbent to plan daily programs of work, maintain accurate records and allow easy updating and retrieval of stored data.
Offer Details 
The commencing salary for this position is up to $54.95 per hour (inclusive of 25% casual loading). Central Coast Council also provides progression opportunities for employees to progress up to the maximum salary of $66.05 per hour on completion of assessment of skills and/ or performance plus 12% superannuation 
- We have casual positions available
- This role is located at Council's Charmhaven and Kincumber Sewerage Treatment Plants.
Want to know more?
The contact person for this role is Jake Nilson, Team Leader Laboratory. You can contact Jake on 0431174539.
This position will close for applications at midnight on Sunday, 29 November 2026.
We will not accept unsolicited resumes or applications being presented by recruitment agencies.
